append.text: **Ps 77:38 *et propítius fiet peccátis eórum* → *e será clemente com os pecados deles*** (decision `propitius`) — Ps 78's proposal taken for the family where the object is a sin, as this row asked after 64:4. **Tested: the ambiguity reader heard 'will forgive their sins' first, 'be lenient toward them' second — no reading of favouring sin**; the Latinist passed it on both drafts; the stylist did not remark. *misericordioso* (miséricors) stands in the same line and stays apart. Options *será propício aos* (24:11 / 64:4's build), *perdoará* (dimíttere's). 24:11, 64:4 and 102:3 still await Gustavo's ruling on the family.

**Ps 77:2 *loquar propositiónes ab inítio* → *falarei o que foi proposto desde o princípio*** — the row's test: *o que proponho desde o princípio* would tie *ab inítio* to my speaking, so the clause turns passive (the old things were put forward). Both Latinist runs (minor) asked the noun *proposições* (parallel to *parábolis*); the ambiguity reader heard 'something planned long ago'. Held under D43; *proposições*, *o que proponho* and *enigmas* are options — for Gustavo.

**Ps 77:8 *generátio prava et exásperans* → *geração perversa e que exaspera*** — absolute, as 67:7b; *exasperante* is 'annoying' in Brazil. The stylist asked *provocadora* — refused (*provocar* is exacerbáre's, D27); the ambiguity reader heard no object, as the Latin. 77:40 *exacerbavérunt* stays *provocaram* (D27) though its Greek is παραπικραίνω — the Latin verb rules.
**Ps 77:17 *apposuérunt adhuc peccáre* → *tornaram ainda a pecar*** — *tornar a* (76:8's draft 1), because *voltar* is convértere's three times in Ps 77 (77:9, 34, 41). Passed all readers.

**Ps 77:31 *occídit pingues eórum* → *matou os mais robustos dentre eles*** (v2) — v1 *os gordos* was heard as comic, literally fat people, by the stylist and the ambiguity reader; the gate Latinist (minor) asked *os gordos* back — held, option. A local departure for persons; 21:30 stands. For Gustavo.

**Ps 77:46 *labóres eórum* → *os seus trabalhos*; 77:51 *primítias omnis labóris eórum* → *as primícias de todo o seu trabalho*** (v2) — the product of toil; *fadigas* was heard as tiredness given to the locust. A local departure; *fadiga* the option.

**Ps 77:48 *possessiónem eórum igni* → *os seus bens ao fogo*** (v2, decision `possessio`) — the Latinist and the stylist heard *posse* as the right of owning, not the goods (ὕπαρξιν); the Latinist's *possessão* is demonic possession in Brazil. *posse* stays for the land (2:8).
Ps 77:26 *Tránstulit Austrum de cælo* → *Fez passar do céu o vento sul* (v2) — the Greek is ἀπῆρεν, not 45:3's μετατίθεσθαι, so D15 lets it differ; the stylist heard *Transportou* as freight. Option.
Ps 77:50 *in morte conclúsit* → *encerrou na morte*; 77:62 *conclúsit in gládio* → *encerrou … na espada* — the ambiguity reader heard *encerrou* as 'ended' at 77:62; kept, *sob a espada* option.

Ps 77:44 *convértit in sánguinem* → *converteu em sangue*. **77:57 *convérsi sunt in arcum pravum* → *se tornaram um arco torto*** (v2, decision `conversi`) — of people, *converter-se* was heard by the stylist and the ambiguity reader as religious conversion; with the Latinist's grammar (the fathers the subject).
Ps 77:29 applied (*não foram privados do seu desejo*).
Ps 77:27 *volatília pennáta* → *aves aladas* — *penas* avoided as this row warns.

terms: | excitáre / excitári | despertar (*despertaram o Excelso para a ira … E o Senhor despertou como quem dormia*) | open | Ps 77:17, 77:65 — one verb so the psalm's echo is heard (they rouse God; God rouses himself). v1 *despertaram a ira do Excelso*; the Latinist asked God as object — v2 the Latin build. *excitar* has sexual senses in Brazil. Kept apart from *in iram concitáre* → *incitar à ira* (77:40, 58). Other places not yet counted (grep before ruling). |

| provocáre ad æmulatiónem | mover ao ciúme (*com as suas imagens esculpidas o moveram ao ciúme*) | open | Ps 77:58 (παρεζήλωσαν; DRB 'moved him to jealousy'); *provocar* is exacerbáre's (D27), *ter inveja* is æmulári's for men (36:1). |

| différre (*audívit … et dístulit*) | adiar (*o Senhor ouviu, e adiou*) | open | Ps 77:21 (ἀνεβάλετο); DRB / MS1932 'was angry' is the Hebrew (rule 1). The ambiguity reader found *adiou* senseless beside the fire — so is the Latin at first hearing. |
| impedíre | entravar (*e entravou os escolhidos de Israel*) | open | Ps 77:31 (συνεπόδισεν, fettered the feet). Unknown to the ambiguity reader; *derrubar* is supplantáre's. |

| abundáre ut | ser abundante em (*E foi abundante em desviar a sua ira*) | open | Ps 77:38b (πληθυνεῖ τοῦ ἀποστρέψαι); v1 *muitas vezes* (DRB, MS1932) was the Latinist's minor as the Hebrew's reading. |

| cœnomyía / ærúgo / morus | a mosca canina / ferrugem / amoreiras | open | Ps 77:45–47, the Latin's (Greek) creatures and plants: κυνόμυια, ἐρυσίβη (the crop blight, also *ferrugem*), συκάμινος. DRB's 'divers sorts of flies' and MS1932's *sicómoros* refused. *mosca canina* and *amoreiras* unknown to the ambiguity reader. |

| immissiónes (per ángelos malos) | *o que enviou por meio de anjos maus* | open | Ps 77:49; the noun as a clause (D16) so *Misit … immissiónes* stays one root. Both Latinist runs (minor) asked *envios* — held, option. The ambiguity reader heard demons (the Latin allows it). |
| sors (dividing land) | por sorteio (*repartiu-lhes a terra por sorteio*) | open | Ps 77:54b (v2); *por sorte* was heard as 'by luck'. *funículus distributiónis* → *a corda da distribuição*. |

| Ps 77 names | Efraim (*Ephrem* 77:9 and *Éphraim* 77:67), Jacó, Egito, Tânis, Cam, Silo, José, Judá, Sião, Davi; the winds *Auster / Áfricus* → *o vento sul / o vento sudoeste* | open | Ps 77; *Tânis*, *Cam*, *Silo* unknown to the ambiguity reader (*Silo* heard as a grain silo) — kept. |
